pages.title: CInode and inode types: inode_t, InodeStore, old inodes, backtraces, per-inode locks and caps

features.name: inode_t persistent inode record
features.description: Per-inode record with ~40 fields (ino, rdev, ctime/btime/mtime/atime, mode/uid/gid, nlink, dir_layout, file layout, old_pools, size, truncate_*, time_warp_seq, inline_data, change_attr, client_ranges, dirstat, rstat, accounted_rstat, quota, export pins, flags, version, xattr_version, backtrace_version, scrub stamps, stray_prior_path, fscrypt blobs, optmetadata). Encoded v20/compat6; decoder declares 19.
features.notes: The Rust MDS may choose any on-disk format; the client-visible subset is fixed by InodeStat/MClientCaps.

features.name: Special inode number layout
features.description: Root=1, .ceph=2 (legacy, hidden), global snaprealm=3, lost+found=4, ~mdsR=0x100+R, journals 0x200+R, journal backup 0x300+R, journal pointer 0x400+R, purge queue 0x500+R, strays 0x600+R*10+i, system base 0x1000; normal inodes from (rank+1)<<40 InoTable ranges.
features.notes: Clients reject [0x100,0x1000); root=1 and realm ino 3 are visible to clients.

features.name: Private inode protection
features.description: LOOKUPINO on a private ino returns -ESTALE; setattr on non-base system inodes -EPERM; namespace changes in system dirs other than root -EROFS (except unlink in lost+found); snapshots in system dirs -EPERM.

features.name: Head vs snapped CInodes and multiversion inodes
features.description: A CInode covers [first,last]; head inodes have last=NOSNAP and live in inode_map, snapped ones in snap_inode_map. Directories, realm roots, hard-linked and already-multiversion inodes keep old_inodes (map last->old_inode_t) inside the head; plain files are COWed into separate CInodes.
features.notes: Needed only if snapshots are supported.

features.name: Projection (read-copy-update) of inode, xattrs and snaprealm
features.description: project_inode copies the newest inode_t (and optionally xattrs / sr_t) into a per-inode FIFO projected list; the mutation edits the copy, journals it, and MutationImpl::apply pops the front node and swaps it in, marking dirty and dirty-parent.
features.notes: FIFO pop relies on per-inode journal completion order. Only Server::_rename_apply pops explicitly; unlink/rename may apply a projected snaprealm early (early_pop_projected_snaprealm). prepare_new_srnode for an inode without a realm takes seq from the global snaprealm, current_parent_since from get_oldest_snap(), and only change_attr from the containing realm.

features.name: Inode versioning and client-visible version
features.description: inode.version is drawn from the parent dirfrag's projected_version via pre_dirty: CDir::pre_dirty(min) sets projected_version = max(projected_version, inode's own projected version) + 1, so per-inode versions stay monotonic across renames; clients receive 2*version+projected and apply attributes only from auth replies with a larger version.
features.notes: Clients only need per-inode monotonicity and the odd/even projected convention.

features.name: Dirty-state tracking and log segment membership
features.description: STATE_DIRTY (dirty_inodes), STATE_DIRTYPARENT/DIRTYPOOL (dirty_parent_inodes), STATE_DIRTYRSTAT (parent dirfrag dirty_rstat_inodes), scatter-dirty flags (dirty_dirfrag_* lists) with matching pins; segments cannot expire until the inode is committed and its backtrace stored.

features.name: Base inode objects
features.description: Root and ~mdsN inodes are stored as <ino>.00000000.inode objects (magic 'ceph fs volume v011' + InodeStore v6) by write_full; fetch also reads the legacy 'inode' xattr.
features.notes: On-disk format free for the Rust MDS.

features.name: Inode persistence inside dirfrag omap
features.description: Primary dentry omap value = first + 'i' + {alternate_name, InodeStore-style body v6}; legacy 'I' marker; commit encodes the stable inode pointers off mds_lock.

features.name: Backtraces (parent xattr)
features.description: inode_backtrace_t {ino, ancestors [(dirino,dname,version)], pool, old_pools} stored as xattr 'parent' (plus 'layout', and 'symlink' when mds_symlink_recovery) on <ino>.00000000 in the backtrace pool (metadata pool for dirs, layout pool otherwise) and, when the pool changed (STATE_DIRTYPOOL), in each old pool; written lazily at log-segment expiry as one BatchCommitBacktrace per pool (old-pool updates are separate entries with their own auth pin), issued from the finisher without mds_lock with op priority scaled LOW..HIGH by the trim backlog. open_ino reads 'parent' from the caller's pool or the default data pool, follows bt.pool, then falls back to the metadata pool.
features.notes: Backtraces are the C++ mechanism behind LOOKUPINO/open_ino; a Rust MDS needs some ino-to-location index but the format is free. _stored_backtrace treats -ENOENT as success only if the current backtrace pool is gone; an -ENOENT from a deleted old pool goes to handle_write_error (code reading).

features.name: Default data pool backtrace objects
features.description: Files and mknod nodes created in a non-default pool get the default (first) data pool in old_pools and are marked dirty_pool, so a backtrace object also exists in the default data pool; every non-directory inode gets a head object <ino>.00000000. old_pools never shrinks; purge removes <ino>.00000000 from every old pool.
features.notes: Operational expectation documented in doc/cephfs/createfs.rst; not a client contract, but open_ino starts its backtrace search in the default data pool.

features.name: Directory backtrace verification
features.description: When mds_verify_backtrace>0 the dirfrag fetch also reads the dir's parent xattr; mismatches re-mark the backtrace dirty (assert if >1).

features.name: Per-inode lock set
features.description: 11 locks per CInode: quiescelock and versionlock (LocalLockC), authlock, linklock, xattrlock, snaplock, flocklock, policylock (SimpleLock), filelock (ScatterLock with sm_filelock), nestlock and dirfragtreelock (ScatterLock). Each protects a field group; four (auth, link, xattr, file) back client caps with shifts 2/4/6/8.
features.notes: Cap bit layout is a client contract; internal lock design is free.

features.name: Implicit versionlock and quiescelock acquisition
features.description: acquire_locks adds a versionlock wrlock (leader) or xlock (peer) for every xlock of an auth inode lock, and a quiescelock wrlock for the first cap-bearing wr/xlock in the vector.

features.name: Lock-state payloads for replicas
features.description: encode_lock_state ships per-lock field subsets to replicas (iauth, ilink, idft, ifile, inest, ixattr, isnap, iflock, ipolicy); replicas rebuild an inode_t copy; scatter locks carry replica dirfrag stats back to the auth.
features.notes: btime/change_attr are not in any payload.

features.name: Scatter-gather of dirstat and rstat
features.description: start_scatter, finish_scatter_update (journals accounted updates), finish_scatter_gather_update (folds dirfrag deltas into the inode, checks sums, repairs, broadcasts quota).
features.notes: Directory size and nlink shown to users derive from dirstat.

features.name: Client capability table on the inode
features.description: client_caps map, add_client_cap (PIN_CAPS, realm membership, cap_id), remove_client_cap (releases advisory locks of that client), reconnect_cap, export/clear caps, move_to_realm.

features.name: Loner (exclusive client) selection
features.description: calc_ideal_loner/choose_ideal_loner/try_drop_loner/set_loner_cap pick a single non-stale client wanting write or Fr caps (files) or the only client of a non-subtree-root dir; the loner gets loner-mode caps (e.g. Fx, Ax).
features.notes: Performance feature; correctness only needs the cap rules.

features.name: Allowed/issued/wanted cap computation
features.description: get_caps_liked/allowed_ever/allowed_by_type/careful/xlocker_mask/allowed_for_client, get_caps_issued, get_caps_wanted, issued_caps_need_gather; directory dir-op mask, inline/pool_ns feature gating, quiesce mask (ANY_RD|Fc|Fb|p) and quarantine mask (p only).
features.notes: get_caps_allowed_ever is not masked by the quiesce/quarantine masks; get_caps_careful and get_xlocker_mask do not include p.

features.name: Notable caps and OpenFileTable tracking
features.description: num_caps_notable (caps wanting write or Fr, plus replica wants) and STATE_CLIENTWRITEABLE drive OpenFileTable add/remove for faster recovery.

features.name: InodeStat encoding for replies
features.description: encode_inodestat chooses stable vs projected values per lock group for the requesting client, includes xattrs/inline data only when the client lacks them, issues caps, enforces readdir byte budgets (-ENOSPC), and encodes v9 (REPLY_ENCODING) or legacy feature-gated layout.
features.notes: Bit-exact contract.

features.name: Inode fields in MClientCaps
features.description: encode_cap_message fills layout, size, truncate_*, fscrypt blobs, times, change_attr, time_warp_seq, nfiles/nsubdirs, inline data, max_size, mode/uid/gid, nlink and xattrs (when Xs pending and newer).

features.name: Stat of snapshotted inodes
features.description: For snapid != NOSNAP the auth answers from old_inodes or snapped CInodes, adds snap_btime and snap_metadata from SnapInfo, and grants read-only caps without changing issued state.

features.name: Extended attributes storage and versioning
features.description: xattr map (string -> bufferptr) shared via shared_ptr<const>, xattr_version bumped on every change, MDSMap max_xattr_size (64 KiB default) enforced; xattrlock protects them.
features.notes: Linux xattrs; not core POSIX but expected by clients.

features.name: optmetadata: charmap (case-insensitive/normalized directories)
features.description: CHARMAP opt (casesensitive, normalization=nfd, encoding=utf8) set only on empty dirs without snapshots, inherited by mkdir, sent in InodeStat v8; libcephfs folds names, kernel skips the field. In charmap dirs openc/mkdir/symlink/link/rename return -EPERM unless the session advertises CephFS feature bit 22 (CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP).
features.notes: The kernel snapshot advertises bit 22 as CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS (linux/fs/ceph/mds_client.h:40), so kernels pass the charmap gate without folding names.

features.name: optmetadata: quarantine flag
features.description: QUARANTINE opt on a subvolume root (enabled + timestamp); is_under_quarantine walks realms; caps restricted to p for sessions without quarantine access; replicas react via ipolicy payload.

features.name: Inline data
features.description: inline_data_t {version, data}; CEPH_INLINE_NONE when disabled or unsupported; clients update via cap flush; scrub can uninline.
features.notes: Deprecated feature; only if MDSMap inline_data is enabled.

features.name: fscrypt metadata
features.description: fscrypt_auth (authlock), fscrypt_file (filelock) opaque blobs set at create, by setattr (allow_all caps) or cap flush; fscrypt_last_block blob drives last-block rewrite on truncation; change_attr checked (-EAGAIN).
features.notes: Size bound uses sizeof(ceph_fscrypt_last_block_header) = 32 (unpacked, LP64) while the kernel's packed header is 26 bytes.

features.name: Truncation state
features.description: truncate() sets truncate_from/size/seq++/pending++ and max_size_ever; MDCache truncates objects then truncate_inode_finish clears pending; shrinking setattr waits on WAIT_TRUNC.
features.notes: truncate_seq is carried in client OSD ops.

features.name: Writable ranges / max_size
features.description: client_ranges per client (range.last = max_size, follows); InodeStat/MClientCaps carry min(stable, projected) range.

features.name: Timestamps, time_warp_seq and change_attr
features.description: ctime/mtime/atime/btime updates (setattr, cap flush newer-wins rules), time_warp_seq bump on explicit time set, change_attr monotonic counter exposed to clients (NFS change attribute, fscrypt checks).

features.name: Directory nlink convention
features.description: Directories report nlink 1 (0 when removed); clients synthesize 2+subdirs; libcephfs aborts on other values.

features.name: Directory hash and fragtree exposure
features.description: dir_layout.dl_dir_hash (default rjenkins) and dirfragtree are sent to clients, which hash names to pick frags/MDS and to order hashed readdir.
features.notes: The kernel uses the VFS dcache hash for dl_dir_hash 0/1 while the MDS uses ceph_str_hash(CEPH_STR_HASH_LINUX); only other ids (default 2, rjenkins) agree. Rejoin asserts the loaded hash equals mds_default_dir_hash (MDCache.cc:6137).

features.name: File layout and layout inheritance
features.description: Files carry file_layout_t (inherited from nearest ancestor dir with a layout, else default on first data pool); changeable only while empty; dir layouts via ceph.dir.layout under policylock.
features.notes: Clients need the layout to address data objects.

features.name: Export pins and ephemeral pins on inodes
features.description: export_pin, export_ephemeral_random_pin, distributed pin flag; get_export_pin inheritance; queue_export_pin into MDCache::export_pin_queue; ephemeral pin state bits.
features.notes: dir_pin is reported in InodeStat v2.

features.name: Quiesce block flag and quiescelock
features.description: F_QUIESCE_BLOCK flag (ceph.quiesce.block) and the quiescelock superlock; is_quiesced masks caps; will_block_for_quiesce.

features.name: Auth pins, inode freezing and ambiguous auth
features.description: can_auth_pin/auth_pin with nested counts to parents; freeze_inode/freeze_auth_pin only for cross-MDS rename (peer rename prep freezes the source inode; peer auth-pin requests with auth_pin_freeze freeze its auth pins; rejoin restores frozen auth pins); cap export uses STATE_EXPORTINGCAPS instead; STATE_AMBIGUOUSAUTH and WAIT_SINGLEAUTH.

features.name: Reference pins and orphan purge trigger
features.description: PIN_* reference counts (with per-type ref_map), first_get/last_put pin the primary dentry, STATE_ORPHAN makes _put() trigger stray evaluation when only dirty pins remain.
features.notes: Unlinked-but-open files must survive until last close (POSIX).

features.name: Replication and migration encodings
features.description: _encode_base/_decode_base, encode_replica_inode (base + replica lock states + state), rejoin lock states, encode_export/finish_export/decode_import with MASK_STATE_EXPORTED/EXPORT_KEPT.

features.name: Scrub validation of inodes
features.description: validate_disk_state compares on-disk vs in-memory backtrace (optionally sets scrub_tag), repairs backtraces and InoTable, checks dirfrag stat sums for directories, and only for base directories (root, ~mdsN) compares the on-disk .inode via a shadow CInode; other inodes get no on-disk inode check (TODO in code).

features.name: Inode admin dumps
features.description: dump inode, dump tree, dump cache, openfiles ls, dump stray print CInode::dump / inode_t::dump JSON.
features.notes: Used by QA tests, not by mgr modules.

features.name: Inode-related perf counters
features.description: mds.inodes (actually dentry LRU size), inodes_with_caps, inodes_expired, mds_mem.ino/ino+/ino-, openino_backtrace_fetch and scrub_* counters.
features.notes: mgr prometheus/dashboard read daemon perf counters (unverified which ones they use).

features.name: Getattr/lookup batching on inodes
features.description: CInode::batch_ops (and CDentry::batch_ops) collect identical getattr/lookup requests by mask so one does the locking and all are answered.
features.notes: mds_allow_batched_ops default true.

features.name: stray_prior_path recording
features.description: Path before unlink/rename-over is stored in the inode for stray diagnostics.

features.name: Async-create cap id convention
features.description: Caps created for an inode allocated by the same request get cap_id 1, matching the kernel's fabricated inode for async creates.
features.notes: Only with async dirops (delegated inos).

features.name: subvolume_id exposure
features.description: InodeStat v9 and cap acks carry the containing realm's (outermost) subvolume ino; kernel requires immutability per inode.
features.notes: Used for per-subvolume client metrics.

features.name: Shared MDS value types (mdstypes.h)
features.description: feature_bitset_t (u32 byte length + LE u64 blocks), metric_spec_t, client_metadata_t v3, session_info_t v7/c7, cap_reconnect_t v2, snaprealm_reconnect_t v1, dirfrag_t, dentry_key_t naming (name_head / name_<hex snap>), load vectors, MDSCacheObjectInfo, BlockDiff, SubvolumeMetric.
features.notes: Wire-relevant ones are client contracts; others are internal.

features.name: Popularity vectors on inodes
features.description: inode_load_vec_t pop (2 decay counters) on each CInode, exported with the inode; dirfrag_load_vec_t meta_load weights 1/2/1/2/4.

serialization_points.name: All CInode state under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: entire cache incl. every CInode field, lock, cap and list
serialization_points.why_serialized: single big lock design; CInode has no own mutex
serialization_points.notes: True conflicts are per inode and per lock/field group.

serialization_points.name: Per-inode projected_nodes FIFO
serialization_points.why_serialized: commit must pop in projection order; relies on ordered journal completion
serialization_points.notes: Same-inode ordering is inherent; dependence on one global journal is not. The MDLog submit thread encodes the projected inode with no lock held (submit_mutex is released before encode_with_header, MDLog.cc:518-525).

serialization_points.name: Inode version from parent dirfrag counter
serialization_points.why_serialized: dentry/inode/dirfrag versions share one sequence for commit bookkeeping
serialization_points.notes: Siblings in one dirfrag contend on one counter.

serialization_points.name: Parent inode projection for dirstat/rstat
serialization_points.shared_state: parent directory inode (and ancestors) projected inode, dirfrag fnode
serialization_points.why_serialized: every create/unlink/size change projects the parent inode and dirfrag; ancestors throttled by mds_dirstat_min_interval
serialization_points.notes: Counts/rctime are commutative deltas or max-merges.

serialization_points.name: versionlock auto-acquisition
serialization_points.why_serialized: leader wrlock to pipeline journaled updates; peer xlock blocks all other updates for rollback safety

serialization_points.name: quiescelock superlock
serialization_points.why_serialized: quiesce must block new cap-related writers and cap issue
serialization_points.notes: Scope extends to a subtree through the QuiesceDb.

serialization_points.name: Cap-bearing lock states vs issued caps
serialization_points.why_serialized: lock transitions must wait for client cap revocation

serialization_points.name: Ancestor snaplock/policylock rdlocks
serialization_points.shared_state: snaplock and policylock of every ancestor
serialization_points.why_serialized: snapshot/layout/quota consistency for the duration of an op
serialization_points.notes: Conflicts only with mksnap/layout/quota/pin changes on ancestors.

serialization_points.name: Backtrace batching at segment expiry
serialization_points.why_serialized: backtraces must be stored before the journal segment can be trimmed

serialization_points.name: Path-string construction in quarantine-aware cap math
serialization_points.shared_state: CPU time under mds_lock; session map
serialization_points.why_serialized: MDS auth caps are path based; recomputed per client per evaluation

serialization_points.name: Nested auth pins and inode freeze
serialization_points.shared_state: auth_pins counters on inode and ancestors' dentries/dirs
serialization_points.why_serialized: migration and cross-MDS rename need quiescence

serialization_points.name: Pending truncation ordering
serialization_points.why_serialized: object truncations must be applied in order

serialization_points.name: Global waiter sequence
serialization_points.why_serialized: ordering of waiters across all cache objects
serialization_points.notes: Must become per-object or atomic without mds_lock.

serialization_points.name: Global inode bookkeeping
serialization_points.shared_state: inode_map, snap_inode_map, num_inodes_with_caps, last_cap_id, Counter<CInode> atomics

serialization_points.name: Scatter accounted-stat journaling
serialization_points.why_serialized: replica/auth must journal accounted updates before the lock cycles

external_contract.detail: Never return inode numbers in [0x100, 0x1000); the kernel refuses them with -EREMOTEIO (warns for >= 0x200).
Client::is_reserved_vino rejects MDS_IS_PRIVATE_INO numbers.
Root directory is ino 1 (CEPH_INO_ROOT).
Realm ino 3 (CEPH_INO_GLOBAL_SNAPREALM) appears in realm references; libcephfs pins that realm until unmount.

With REPLY_ENCODING: ENCODE_START(9,1); kernel requires struct_compat == 1 and struct_v >= 1, reads packed ceph_mds_reply_inode then fragtree splits, symlink, dir layout, xattr blob, inline, quota (v1/compat 1), pool_ns, btime, change_attr, dir_pin, snap_btime, rsnaps, snap_metadata, fscrypt flag/blobs, optmetadata (skipped), subvolume_id; trailing bytes are skipped.
InodeStat::decode for v9 and legacy feature-gated layout.
Attributes applied when i_version==0 or the reply carries CEPH_CAP_FLAG_AUTH and version > (cached & ~1); MDS sends 2*v + projected.
Same rule as the kernel in Client::add_update_inode.
Directory inodes must have nlink 0 or 1; any other value hits ceph_abort() in fill_stat.
nlink 1 is reported as 2+subdirs; st_size = files + subdirs from dirstat, or rbytes with the rbytes mount option, or the snapshot count for .snap.

dir_layout.dl_dir_hash selects ceph_str_hash (ids >= 2) or the VFS dcache hash (0/1) for frag choice and hashed readdir; the MDS maps 0/1 to ceph_str_hash_linux, so only ids >= 2 (default 2, rjenkins) hash identically on both sides.
Used as monotonic i_version (STATX_ATTR_CHANGE_MONOTONIC, NFS change attribute).

Shrinking setattr carries ceph_fscrypt_truncate_size_header + last block; MDS answers -EAGAIN if change_attr mismatches, -EINVAL if payload > header + mds_fscrypt_last_block_max_size; MDS later rewrites the last block.
A non-zero subvolume_id must never change for an inode (kernel WARN).
Kernel fabricates async-created inodes with cap_id 1, version 1, truncate_seq 1, truncate_size -1, xattr_version 1; MDS uses cap_id 1 for inodes created by the request.
u32 count + (u32 len key, u32 len value)*; blob sent only when xattr_version is newer than the client's or Xs requested; xattr_version 0 means no blob.
CHARMAP drives client name normalization/case-folding; QUARANTINE marks quarantined inodes.

external_contract.item: Cap bit layout per inode lock
external_contract.detail: As/Ax shift 2, Ls/Lx 4, Xs/Xx 6, file bits shift 8; quiesce mask ANY_RD|Fc|Fb|p; quarantine mask p.
Grant/revoke/trunc/import messages carry layout, size, truncate_seq/size, times, change_attr, time_warp_seq, nfiles/nsubdirs, inline data, max_size, mode/uid/gid, nlink, xattrs.

ctime/change_attr newer-wins; mtime newer-wins with Fw, any with Fx; size only grows; atime/time_warp_seq with Fx; uid/gid/mode/btime/fscrypt_auth with Ax; xattrs with Xx and newer xattr_version. With Ax the client's whole mode (including S_IFMT bits) is copied unmasked.
create(non-exclusive) + setxattr parent/layout/symlink on <ino>.00000000 in data/metadata pools, empty SnapContext; getxattr parent reads.
write_full of <ino>.00000000.inode in the metadata pool; read of legacy 'inode' xattr.
cephfs-data-scan, cephfs-journal-tool, cephfs-meta-injector and ceph-dencoder decode inode_t, InodeStore(Bare), inode_backtrace_t and parent/layout/scrub_tag xattrs.

external_contract.item: dump inode / dump tree / openfiles ls / dump stray
external_contract.detail: JSON field names from inode_t::dump and CInode::dump; used by QA tests.
mds.inodes (dentry LRU size), inodes_with_caps, mds_mem.ino etc. are exported as daemon perf counters.
NFS file handles carry inos; LOOKUPINO must resolve any live ino, including uncached ones (C++ uses backtraces via open_ino).

The kernel advertises bit 22 as CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS; the userspace MDS reads bit 22 as CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP and uses it to allow namespace ops in charmap directories (Server::can_handle_charmap).
Purging a file removes <ino>.00000000 in its layout pool (when not covered by the range purge) and in every pool listed in old_pools.

rust_implications.implication: Allocate inode numbers outside [0x100,0x1000) (clients refuse that range); keep root=1 and use 3 (or another fixed ino) consistently as the global realm ino if snapshots are offered; per-shard ino ranges can replace the per-rank (rank+1)<<40 InoTable ranges since they are not visible to clients except through delegated ranges.

Keep a per-inode monotonic version and send 2*v+1 when the reply contains uncommitted (projected) values for the requester; there is no need to derive it from the parent dirfrag counter, which removes sibling contention.

The C++ shared_ptr<const inode_t> RCU pattern maps directly to Arc<InodeData>; journal encoding, dirfrag/object commits and backtrace writes can then run on worker threads without any lock, as C++ already does for three paths.

Per-inode pending-update queues must commit in projection order; with per-shard journals all updates of one inode must go through one shard (or carry sequence numbers) and cross-shard ops (rename) need 2PC that respects each inode's queue.

Map the 4 cap-bearing field groups (auth: mode/uid/gid/btime/fscrypt_auth; link: nlink; xattr: xattrs/xattr_version; file: size/times/layout/truncate/client_ranges/inline/fscrypt_file) onto independent locks; the cap shift layout is a wire contract, the internal lock implementation is free.

Directory nlink must be reported as 0/1 and dirstat nfiles/nsubdirs must be accurate enough for st_size and nlink synthesis; rstat/dirstat propagation can be done with commutative per-shard deltas instead of projecting parent inodes on every create.

Clients never read backtraces, but LOOKUPINO (NFS handles, ceph_ll_lookup_inode) requires resolving any live ino; a Rust MDS needs an ino->parent index (sharded omap index or backtraces); writing backtraces to data-pool head objects costs one extra OSD op per new inode and is only needed for cephfs-data-scan compatibility.
Implement encode with ENCODE_START(9,1) (compat must stay 1 for the kernel); new fields may be appended; include dir_layout hash and fragtree consistent with the MDS's own dentry hashing.
Keep an xattr_version per inode and send the blob only when the client lacks it; honor MDSMap max_xattr_size; cap flush with Xx replaces the whole map.

Quiesce and quarantine are expressed as cap masks (ANY_RD|Fc|Fb|p and p) and request blocking; in a sharded design these masks are per-subvolume state that the scheduler can apply without a global lock.
Quarantine-aware cap computation rebuilds the inode path per client; precompute the subvolume membership/quarantine state per shard to avoid O(depth) work per cap evaluation.
A C++ CInode is ~1.3 KB plus ~0.6 KB inode_t (estimate); a Rust design can allocate lock state, cap tables, snapshot data, scrub info and replication state lazily and drop debug ref maps.

Inodes created by a request must get cap_id 1 for the creating client to match kernel async-create fabrication; initial values (truncate_seq 1, truncate_size -1, xattr_version 1, setgid inheritance) must match what the kernel fabricates.
subvolume_id sent to clients must never change for an inode; renames across subvolumes must stay forbidden (EXDEV) to preserve this.
Preserve truncate_seq/truncate_size semantics (clients send truncate_seq with OSD writes) and serialize shrinking truncations per inode.
Unlinked-but-open inodes must stay alive until the last cap/reference is released; tie purge to cap release events per shard instead of a global ref-count hook.
Bump change_attr on every metadata or data-visible change and accept larger client values on cap flush; fscrypt truncation relies on exact change_attr comparison (-EAGAIN on mismatch).
C++ replicas do not receive btime/change_attr updates via lock messages; a Rust design without replicas (autonomous shards) avoids this inconsistency class entirely.

Kernel clients set CephFS feature bit 22 meaning SUBVOLUME_METRICS while the C++ MDS reads bit 22 as CHARMAP; a Rust MDS that serves unmodified kernels must not infer charmap/name-folding support from bit 22 alone (or must accept that C++ behavior and document it).
If C++-compatible backtraces are kept, open_ino-style lookups start in the default data pool, so inodes in other pools need a redirect backtrace there; purge must also delete those old-pool objects.

open_questions: Legacy SETLAYOUT (Server::handle_client_setlayout) calls add_old_pool() before pre_dirty(), so is_backtrace_updated() is false and the op does not dirty the backtrace. Code reading: harmless while the create-time DIRTYPARENT|DIRTYPOOL is still pending; otherwise the new pool lacks a backtrace until a later update_backtrace() mutation, and old pools are never refreshed. Not tested.

optmetadata_singleton::get_kind() uses '>' instead of '>=' against the variant size (3); a kind value of exactly 3 from a newer peer makes defconstruct_type index past its 3-entry table (undefined behavior per code reading; not tested).
acquire_locks adds the quiescelock only for the first cap-related lock per call, while doc/dev/mds_internals/quiesce.rst says every operation; is the per-call behavior intended for multi-inode ops?

encode_inodestat leaves ecap.cap_id and ecap.wanted uninitialized for snapshot stats. The kernel (ceph_fill_inode) and libcephfs (Client::add_update_inode) read them only for CEPH_NOSNAP inodes; other clients (e.g. older kernels) were not checked.
In MDCache::quarantine_inode a non-auth root projects the inode but there is no pop path, and pop_and_apply_projected_inode is unused; verify replica behavior (out of scope here).

Confirmed by code: kernel mds_client.h:40 defines bit 22 as CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS and advertises it; src/mds/cephfs_features.h:53 defines bit 22 as CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP, which Server::can_handle_charmap uses to allow namespace ops in charmap directories. The wire-protocol and metrics pages should record the conflict and its effect on metrics negotiation.
Per-object memory sizes are hand estimates; actual sizeof(CInode)/sizeof(inode_t) were not measured (no build).
Which daemon perf counters (e.g. mds.inodes) are consumed by mgr modules (prometheus/dashboard) is not verified here.
_stored_backtrace's -ENOENT tolerance checks only the current backtrace pool; whether a deleted pool can remain in old_pools of live inodes (and so trigger handle_write_error) was not tested.

optmetadata_singleton::operator== memcmp()s std::string/std::vector objects and padded structs; inode_t::compare (scrub) can report spurious divergence for equal-version inodes with optmetadata (code reading, not tested).
